steps.note: S2.1.3.1 states that rows 0-1 remove the old scratch contributions and rows 6-7 restore the scratch wires, and S2.1.3.2 states the net target change (JV+RG)x independent of the initial side and central values a,c, quoting line 748.

S2.1.3.3 gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, cancellation of exactly the intersection-one cases by the side injection, zero for intersections zero and two, and self coefficient one.
S2.1.3.4 gives the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, cancelled by the side for intersections zero and two, intersection one contributing zero, self coefficient one.
S2.1.3.5 states the three stages forward/inverse/forward sending (x,y) to (x,y+x), (-y,y+x), (-y,x), and S2.1.3 states that the invocations restore every scratch wire whatever its initial value.

The plan says every edge joins comparable labels (S2.1.5.1.3) and gives only the center 3->4 and side 2->5 edges, but never states the per-edge orthogonal residuals and their dimensions (the residual table).

S2.1.5.1.4 states that the side edge 2->5 is nested because t_X is orthogonal to t_Y, so <t_X> is contained in t_Y^perp, quoting line 1048; it does not add that the residual is <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2.

The plan states that only center 3->4 decreases (losing P(x)F(x)Q of dimension h), sources N and sinks Wm-N, the telescoping signed sum Wm-2N, and Ic edges of loss h adding 2L for the absolute budget Wm-2N+2L.

S2.1.5.1.8 states that over F_2 each nonzero residual has an orthonormal basis because it is nondegenerate and nonalternating (contains a norm-one vector); the plane-absorption argument itself is not spelled out.
The plan never states weight additivity modulo four for orthogonal binary vectors or the formula q_V-q_U = sum over an orthonormal residual basis of wt(v)[v.x].
S2.2.1 and S2.2.1.3 assert that each edge's frame change is a product of kernels (aI+bX_v)^{+-1}, but the plan never derives it from wt(v) odd, the phase i^{eps[v.x]}, or H diag(1,-1) H = X.

The plan states one directional kernel per residual basis vector, each realised as a single child (C^{+-1}) tensored over the f columns of a slot, with exactly s_c child calls in all (quoting line 1905 where the paper uses this count).

The plan has no complex endpoint analysis: the zero label's frame I, the full label's C^{(x)m}, C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) repaired by Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}Z_{a,k}, and negation of the X outputs are all missing (only C^{-1}=-iZCZ appears, in S2.2.1.2).
S2.1.5.1.9 says both loss ratios are below 1/2, and S2.1.5.2.3 derives the deficit N-2L_b>0 from L_b<N/2, so s_b<W_b m.
S2.1.5.3.1 names the relative deficit eta_b but never gives its value 339/22587335000000.
S2.1.5.3.1 names eta_c but never gives its value 73/19906842167500.
The plan states that both deficits exceed 20*2^-50, that log m<20, that m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta), and hence s_b/W_b<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^-50.

The plan gives the topmost-row rightmost-entry pivot, clearing left and below by lower-triangular elementary operations, deletion and repetition on the active indices, and a final Pi with exactly a ones.
S2.1.5.5.1 chooses an odd prime avoiding every denominator of the finite table and every diagonal numerator, so the triangular factors stay invertible modulo q^b.
S2.1.5.5.2 states that a lower-triangular transformation costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order from earlier unchanged coordinates.
The plan realises each one of Pi by D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j, yielding (h+d,d) with one interchange each and a in all.
The plan defines E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu=min{j>=1: m^j>=B}, Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) and C_1=20; it does not write C_0=128mB^2 or C_1=max{20,nu+3} (nu=11) explicitly.
The plan states the per-invocation count 24W^3+4s+4W+4<E, the recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e)<=8e at a leaf, and why it uses s rather than s/W.
S2.2.4.4 gives the unrolling with sx+E<=Bx and B^{log_m d+2}<=B^2 d^nu to A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and S2.2.4.5 bounds the total by 128mB^2 d^{nu+3}<=C_0 d^{C_1}.

Only the last part (epsilon C_1<1 gives Delta=o(p), S2.2.4.6) is stated; the induction that depth l gives values in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] of modulus at most 2^l and the reservation of p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are missing, and S2.2.4 only asserts growth by at most Delta bits.
S2.2.7 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and the single truncation errs by less than sqrt(2) 2^-p.

summary: P06 states 19 of 26 sub-steps. The bank-exchange network (B1-B4), the matrix shear (M1-M4) and most of the guard-width chain (S1-S3, S5) are carried step by step with the paper's own lines. The gaps are the residual table (L1), the derivation of the phase interface (P1, P2, P4; only the kernel count P3 is stated), the exact deficit values eta_b and eta_c (R2, R3), and the depth-to-bit-size induction with the bit reservation (S4).
